key_insight: An enhanced physics-informed neural network for quantum optimal control can match classical solvers while suppressing leakage and achieving >99.9% gate fidelity on multi-level quantum hardware models.
engineering_relevance: This work points to a practical path for automating high-fidelity pulse design in scalable quantum processors using physics-guided machine learning.
method: PINNQOC adds Fourier feature embeddings to reduce spectral bias in oscillatory quantum dynamics.
Dynamic epoch normalization and informed pre-training improve training stability under global phase constraints.
The method is benchmarked against Krotov and PRONTO on fluxonium and NV-center gate-control tasks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic comparisons on a truncated three-level fluxonium qubit and a four-level NV center system, with gate fidelities exceeding 99.9% and analysis of computation time, iterations, and mean leakage.
watch_item: PINNs can still be sensitive to training setup and problem scaling, so performance may depend on careful tuning and may not always beat established optimal-control solvers.
paper_title: Performance of Krotov, PRONTO and PINN for optimal control of quantum gates
